findings.breaking_input: A journal line {"work":true,"phase":"apply","ok":true,"receipt":"<id of any decision.recorded event already on the spine>"} on a named day, or an id from a different day. The id is in spine.ids, so opsByDay[day]++ runs. A day with only a decision and no real work-op apply then passes the op clause.
findings.why: The spine check is membership in the set of every event id. It does not check the event kind, that it was written by a work-door apply, that it was written on the same day, or that its op matches. This is the 'printed id credited as a receipt' and 'membership where identity was needed' pattern. The op clause is the new gate, and it is satisfied by any id the journal quotes.
findings.fix: Keep a map from id to {kind, day, op/process}. Count an op only when the event is the work door's apply kind, its day equals the journal line's day, and its payload op matches the journalled op. Add a mutant arm where the receipt is a decision id.
findings.twin_of: A printed id credited as a receipt -> A line in a shared stream proves nothing about who wrote it.

findings.breaking_input: A journal line containing the text `null` (or `1`, `"x"`). JSON.parse succeeds, the new `e && e.work` guard is skipped, and `e.path` on null throws a TypeError. A number or string primitive has no `path`, so it is silently skipped without being counted as torn.
findings.why: The diff guards `e &&` in the new branch but leaves the next line unguarded. A line that is not an object should count as torn. The null case throws out of readJournal instead, so the run dies with an uncaught error rather than exit 2 or a named finding.
findings.fix: After JSON.parse, `if (e === null || typeof e !== "object" || Array.isArray(e)) { torn++; continue; }`.
findings.twin_of: A spine line that parses to a non-object (`null`) was kept as an event -> a JSON line that is not an object is torn, in every engine.

findings.breaking_input: `node face-dogfood.mjs --day 2026-02-30 --json | cat` on Windows with stderr piped. The refusal is written to stderr and then process.exit(2) runs immediately.
findings.why: process.exit() directly after an asynchronous pipe write can truncate or lose the message on Windows. The bats test asserts on that message, so it can flake. The code sets exitCode elsewhere.
findings.fix: Set process.exitCode = 2 and return from the parse (or throw to a single exit path) instead of calling process.exit.
findings.twin_of: `process.exit()` raced libuv teardown on Windows -> set `process.exitCode` and let the loop drain.

findings.breaking_input: `face-dogfood.mjs --days 1 2026-10-13` (the user forgot `--day`). The date is the first non-dash token, so it is taken as the repo root. A second stray positional, such as `repo-a repo-b`, is silently ignored.
findings.why: A mode that ignores what it was given answers a question nobody asked. A mistyped window turns into a read of a nonexistent path or an all-history verdict. A second positional is never refused.
findings.fix: Collect the positionals that no flag consumed. Refuse more than one by name. Refuse a positional that matches the YYYY-MM-DD shape with a hint to use --day.
findings.twin_of: Extra tokens ignored -> A mode that ignores what it was given answers a question nobody asked.

findings.breaking_input: A journal op line whose receipt is "X\nface-dogfood: REQ-10 MET" or contains an ESC or other control character. It is interpolated raw into the reason line and printed to the terminal and the evidence files.
findings.why: The receipt string is read from disk and printed without a one-line or grammar check. A parser of day-N.txt or the summary can see a forged verdict line. The reason prints `${o.receipt}` unquoted.
findings.fix: Print only receipts that match the ULID grammar. Otherwise JSON.stringify them and cap their length. Count malformed receipts as torn at read time.
findings.twin_of: A finding that interpolates a fold-returned string raw -> every value a finding quotes from data is one line, quoted and capped.

findings.breaking_input: `face-dogfood.mjs --day=2026-10-13` or `--days=1`. Nothing in the diff shows refuseUnknownFlags rejecting the `=VALUE` form of a known flag. If it matches on the name before `=`, the value is ignored and the full-history verdict runs.
findings.why: A narrowed window silently falls back to all history. This is the exact opposite of what the caller asked for.
findings.fix: Refuse any `--flag=...` form by name, and add a bats arm with `--day=2026-10-13` that expects exit 2.
findings.twin_of: `--flag=VALUE` accepted and silently ignored -> a flag form the parser does not read is an error, never a no-op.

findings.breaking_input: Delete or fail to register 5 of the new selftest arms. The floor `-ge 29` is hand-kept and was not derived from the registered arms. A removal that leaves at least 29 PASS lines still exits 0, and only the named-arm loop notices some of them.
findings.why: The count floor is a hand-kept number. Several new arms (for example the three `--day` guard arms other than the future one, and the 'outside decision on a named day' arm) have no entry in the named list, so they could silently vanish.
findings.fix: Have the selftest print a RAN: N line derived from its own armed() calls, and have the test compare the PASS count to that N.
findings.twin_of: A hand-kept floor one above the real count -> Never hand-keep a count the code can print.
